documents.title: Neurology follow-up letter
documents.author: neurology
documents.body:
NEUROLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Visit date: 10/31/2022

Mr. Kerrigan returns for REM sleep behavior disorder, first evaluated here in November 2021. His wife says the night-time episodes have grown more frequent and forceful: he punches and kicks while asleep and has come out of bed several times, with some minor bumps and bruises. He has no awareness of these events, though he can recall dreams full of action and confrontation.

Current medications: melatonin 3 mg nightly, metformin 1000 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily. Allergies: none.
Active issues also include type 2 diabetes with retinopathy, hypertension, hyperlipidemia, thoracic spinal stenosis, and a diabetic foot ulcer of the right foot.

Exam: alert and oriented, attentive, normal recall and conversation. No rigidity, no slowing of repetitive movements, no tremor. Gait normal.

The polysomnogram of November 2021 showed REM sleep without atonia; no repeat study is needed.

Assessment and plan: RBD, clinically worse. Increase melatonin to 6 mg at bedtime. Reviewed bedroom safety again; his wife has started sleeping in the guest room on bad nights. Follow-up in 12 months.

(Letter delayed in transcription; we apologize.)

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, high MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
CC: tired, sweats, losing weight.

HPI: 67M. About 7 weeks of feeling worn out by early afternoon, drenching sweats at night a few times a week (changing his T-shirt), eating less, and a full feeling in the belly after small meals. Scale at home down about 10 pounds; today's weight confirms the loss. No fever he's measured, no cough, no bleeding, no change in bowels, no urinary symptoms. Back pain no different. Sleep episodes unchanged on melatonin 6.

Exam: Vitals as charted. Looks tired, a bit pale. Several firm, non-tender, mobile lymph nodes both sides of the neck and in both armpits, 1-2 cm. Abdomen soft, fullness in the LUQ, I think I can feel a spleen tip. No hepatomegaly. Heart regular, lungs clear. No edema. Skin: no petechiae.

CBC with diff and CMP drawn now, asked lab to call.

A/P: Constitutional symptoms with diffuse adenopathy and probable splenomegaly in a man whose uncle had CLL - concerned for a lymphoproliferative disorder. Urgent heme/onc referral placed today; will call him tonight with the CBC.

documents.title: CBC result call
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called pt with CBC: WBC 13.6 with 71% lymphocytes, Hgb 9.4, platelets 156. Explained this fits a blood disorder like the leukemia his uncle had but needs confirmation by hematology. Urgent referral sent; their office will call. Spoke to referral coordinator - appointment 4/27. He and his wife asked good questions. Call sooner for fever, bleeding, worsening breathlessness.

documents.title: Hematology-oncology consultation
documents.author: hematology-oncology
documents.body:
HEMATOLOGY & ONCOLOGY CONSULTATION
Visit: 04/27/2023

Reason for referral: anemia, lymphocytosis and lymphadenopathy.

History: 67-year-old man with type 2 diabetes with retinopathy and a right plantar diabetic foot ulcer, here for two months of fatigue, night sweats and an unintended 10 lb weight loss, along with early fullness and reduced appetite.
Medications: metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, melatonin. NKDA.
Family: maternal uncle with CLL; father with prostate cancer.

Exam: pallor. Bilateral cervical and axillary adenopathy. Spleen palpable 3 cm below the left costal margin. No hepatomegaly.

Labs today: hemoglobin 9.2 g/dL, MCV 85 fL, WBC 14,000/uL, platelets 150,000/uL, LDH elevated. Peripheral smear reviewed personally: mature-appearing small lymphocytes with numerous smudge cells.
Peripheral blood flow cytometry: clonal B-cell population co-expressing CD5 and CD23 with dim CD20, kappa light chain restricted.

Impression: chronic lymphocytic leukemia, Rai stage III by anemia, with B symptoms and splenomegaly - meets criteria for treatment.

Plan: acalabrutinib 100 mg twice daily, to start once the specialty pharmacy completes authorization. Counseled on bruising, bleeding, headache, and infection risk; avoid NSAIDs. CBC every 2 weeks for the first month, then monthly. Return in 6 months, sooner as needed.

Thank you for the prompt referral.

medications.sig: Take 1 tablet by mouth twice daily

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u, first time back since the CLL diagnosis.
On acalabrutinib since mid-May. Tolerating it. Sweats stopped, appetite back, has put on a few pounds. Hematology checking counts monthly.
Diabetes: sugars similar, 150s fasting.

Exam: neck nodes smaller, still palpable on the left. Spleen not felt today. Skin clear. Feet okay.

A/P: CLL - responding, managed by heme/onc. CBC today for our records. DM2 - A1c/BMP. HTN - fine. No NSAIDs, acetaminophen only for the back.

documents.title: Annual Wellness Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
MEDICARE AWV

Interval: CLL on acalabrutinib, energy back to normal, weight regained. Sleep episodes ongoing on melatonin 6 mg; wife sleeps separately some nights. Back pain from stenosis manageable.

Functional: independent. Drives locally. No falls from standing. PHQ-2 1.
Proxy on file (wife).

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Small residual nodes L neck. Lungs clear, heart regular. Feet: monofilament reduced, skin intact.

Prevention: flu, COVID and RSV next month at a nurse visit - discussed that vaccine responses may be blunted on his CLL treatment but still worth giving. Colonoscopy due 2027.
Labs: CMP, lipids, A1c, urine microalbumin. CBC per heme.

RTC January.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Given: high-dose influenza L deltoid; 2023-24 COVID R deltoid; RSV vaccine L deltoid lower site, 1 inch apart. Pt aware arm may be sore. Observed 15 min, fine.

documents.title: Back pain at night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Doctor, my back has been different the last several weeks. It's a steady dull ache in the lower back all the time now, and it's worst at night, keeps me up. Resting doesn't help like it used to. I didn't hurt it. I've also dropped some weight again and had a few sweats. I see the cancer doctor next week on Nov 2 for my regular checkup. Should I come in before that?

documents.title: RE: Back pain at night
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me. Night pain that doesn't ease with rest, plus the weight loss and sweats, is something your oncologist should look at closely next week, and they can order the right scans and blood work. Please tell them exactly what you told me. Acetaminophen as before in the meantime. If you develop weakness in the legs, numbness in the groin, or trouble with bladder or bowels, go to the emergency department right away. I'll watch for their note.

documents.title: Oncology follow-up
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
ONCOLOGY FOLLOW-UP
Date of visit: 11/02/2023

Diagnoses: CLL, Rai III at diagnosis, on acalabrutinib since 05/2023. Type 2 diabetes. Diabetic foot ulcer right foot. RBD. Thoracic spinal stenosis.

Interval: six months since diagnosis. Today he reports a constant, dull low back ache, not relieved by rest and worse at night, without trauma. He has lost 10 lb over the last two months and has occasional night sweats again.

Medications: acalabrutinib 100 mg BID, metformin 1000 mg BID, lisinopril 20 mg daily, hydrochlorothiazide 12.5 mg daily, melatonin. NKDA.

Exam: tender over the lumbar spinous processes, no step-off or deformity. Straight leg raise negative bilaterally. Strength, sensation and reflexes in the legs unremarkable.

Labs today: hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL (improved from 9.2), ESR 70 mm/hr, calcium 10.2 mg/dL, alkaline phosphatase 120 U/L.

Assessment: new inflammatory-pattern back pain with recurrent weight loss and a high ESR. CLL itself is responding, so we need to exclude a second process in the bone.

Plan: whole-body bone scan and CT chest/abdomen/pelvis with contrast, PSA. Continue acalabrutinib. Will call with results.

CC: primary care

reports.text: CT CHEST WITH IV CONTRAST. Indication: CLL, back pain, weight loss. Mildly enlarged bilateral axillary lymph nodes, largest 1.4 cm short axis. Lungs clear without nodules or consolidation. No pleural or pericardial effusion. Heart normal in size. Sclerotic lesions in several thoracic vertebral bodies and in multiple ribs bilaterally.
reports.conclusion: Sclerotic osseous lesions in thoracic vertebrae and ribs, suspicious for metastases. Mild axillary adenopathy in keeping with known CLL.

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH IV CONTRAST. Spleen mildly enlarged, 14.2 cm. Liver normal without focal lesion. Adrenal glands normal. Kidneys enhance symmetrically without hydronephrosis. No abdominal or pelvic lymphadenopathy by size criteria. Bladder unremarkable. Multiple sclerotic lesions in lumbar vertebral bodies and both iliac bones; no pathologic fracture.
reports.conclusion: Sclerotic lesions of the lumbar spine and pelvis, suspicious for osteoblastic metastases. Mild splenomegaly consistent with known CLL. No visceral metastasis.

documents.title: Imaging and PSA results
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
Results packet from oncology, studies of 11/08/2023:

Whole-body bone scan: multiple foci of increased radiotracer uptake in the thoracic and lumbar spine, pelvis and several ribs, in a pattern typical of osseous metastatic disease.
CT chest and CT abdomen/pelvis reports attached.
PSA 64.8 ng/mL.

Note from oncology: findings are concerning for metastatic carcinoma to bone, with prostate the leading possibility. CT-guided bone biopsy is being arranged.

documents.title: Reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Reviewed. Called Francis - oncology had already gone over it with him and his wife. Biopsy scheduled for this week. Offered a visit any time; he'll let me know after the biopsy.

documents.author: RN
documents.body: Spoke with pt. Biopsy of the hip bone in November showed the cancer came from the prostate. Got a hormone shot (leuprolide) at the oncology office about two weeks ago and started abiraterone and prednisone last week. Back pain somewhat better. Asked about blood sugars on the prednisone - fasting a little higher, 170s-180s. Told him we'll update his list once the oncology letter arrives and review the diabetes at his January visit; call sooner for sugars over 300 or symptoms. Records request sent to oncology.

medications.sig: 22.5 mg intramuscularly every 12 weeks at oncology
Take 4 tablets (1000 mg) by mouth once daily on an empty stomach
Take 1 tablet by mouth daily with abiraterone

reports.text: SPECIMEN: left iliac bone, CT-guided core biopsy x3. MICROSCOPIC: cores of bone and marrow largely replaced by infiltrating glands and cords of malignant epithelial cells with prominent nucleoli in a desmoplastic stroma. Background marrow with small mature lymphocytes. IMMUNOHISTOCHEMISTRY: tumor cells positive for NKX3.1 and PSA; negative for TTF-1 and CDX2.
reports.conclusion: Metastatic adenocarcinoma, immunoprofile consistent with prostatic origin.

documents.title: Oncology letter: new diagnosis
documents.author: oncology
documents.body:
ONCOLOGY
Date of letter: 12/08/2023

Dear colleague,

Further to our visit of 11/02, Mr. Kerrigan's workup shows metastatic carcinoma to bone. Bone scan showed widespread osseous uptake in the spine, pelvis and ribs, CT showed corresponding sclerotic lesions without visceral disease, and PSA was 64.8. CT-guided biopsy of the left iliac bone on 11/16/2023 confirmed metastatic adenocarcinoma of prostatic origin (pathology enclosed). He has metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer, alongside his CLL, which continues to respond to acalabrutinib.

Treatment begun:
- Leuprolide 22.5 mg IM every 12 weeks, first dose 11/29/2023.
- Abiraterone 1000 mg daily with prednisone 5 mg daily, started 12/06/2023.
- Acalabrutinib 100 mg twice daily continues.
We will monitor PSA, liver tests, potassium and blood pressure monthly at first. Prednisone may raise his glucose; we would appreciate your help with his diabetes.

Other medications: metformin, lisinopril, hydrochlorothiazide, melatonin. Allergies: NKDA.

Follow-up in 3 months with PSA.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Here with wife. Oncology letter of 12/8 and biopsy reviewed with them. Metastatic prostate cancer to bone, on leuprolide, abiraterone and prednisone 5 since late Nov/early Dec. CLL controlled on acalabrutinib. He's taking it in stride; back pain much improved since the hormone shot. Weight down from the fall.
Sugars: fasting 160s-180s since starting prednisone.

Meds reconciled: metformin 1000 BID, lisinopril 20, HCTZ 12.5, melatonin 6 qhs, acetaminophen PRN, acalabrutinib 100 BID, abiraterone 1000 daily, prednisone 5 daily, leuprolide q12 wks.

Exam: vitals per chart. Comfortable. Mild tenderness low lumbar. Lungs clear. Feet intact, monofilament reduced.

A/P:
1. Metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma, bone - per oncology. Problem list updated.
2. CLL - stable.
3. DM2 with retinopathy - A1c today; continue metformin.
4. HTN - continue; oncology also watching BP/K on abiraterone.
RTC April.

Oncology note, 12/04/2024.
Problems: metastatic prostate adenocarcinoma to bone on ADT plus abiraterone/prednisone since 11/2023; CLL on acalabrutinib since 05/2023; diabetic foot ulcer, right foot; type 2 diabetes.
Doing well. No bone pain. PSA undetectable (<0.1). CBC normal with normal lymphocyte count. LFTs and potassium normal. BP acceptable.
Plan: continue leuprolide q12 weeks, abiraterone 1000 mg with prednisone 5 mg, acalabrutinib 100 mg BID. Return 6 months.
